Physical route comparison: ranking gains have not yet reduced fleet cost
1 October 2026 UTC

The first physical comparison covers 16 exploratory training timetables, using models fitted without each timetable’s outer fold. It compares learned route proposals with a fixed policy that reuses existing plans and optimizes their charging. It is not a final test-set evaluation.

On the 15 timetables where all four methods produced a feasible fleet, mean cost differences relative to that reuse policy were +0.48 for the tabular model, +2.83 for the tree-family policy, +4.60 for the graph policy and +21.62 for the cost-only construction. Positive means more expensive. The graph model’s earlier edge-ranking improvement has therefore not yet translated into a general physical cost benefit. The tabular model was closest to reuse on these common cases; its mean across all 16 cases was +7.57 because the extra case was much worse. No model is promoted on these exploratory outcomes.

Independent replay reproduced all 143 saved fleet-plan costs exactly. Primary proposals were feasible on 16/16 cases for the tabular method and 15/16 for each other method. Three cover repairs reached their five-second limit without an integer solution on the same timetable. Raw edge-by-edge predictions formed a valid topology in only 2 of 48 diagnostics, reinforcing the need for explicit route construction and physical replay. Tiny charging differences around 10^-14 are identified separately from meaningful improvements.

The global-bound comparison is incomplete: all 32 hull calls stopped before optimization because the caller used an unsupported keyword. These failures are preserved; successful Slurm completion does not certify the experiment. The completed batch used 1,484 allocated CPU-seconds. Failed attempts and the earlier source-plan acquisition cost remain in the ledger; no optimality or online speedup claim is made.

The longer graph-training batch separately failed during shell startup, before any training, using 12 allocated CPU-seconds. A reviewed startup-only correction was submitted as array 738226 at 02:49 UTC, in a fresh output directory. The scientific settings remain unchanged: up to 900 epochs, the original 300-epoch comparison checks, 12 tasks, at most four concurrent, and a new 12 CPU-hour ceiling. Submission is confirmed; allocation has not yet been observed.

Next, evaluate whether longer training helps, then test physical-context inputs and route construction that accounts for cost under a separate frozen protocol. Keep development and final test timetables sealed. The failed hull interface also needs a separate bounded repair; it is not silently rerun.
